subject: Sunrise notice activation — auto-renew & termination mechanics
messages:
From: Sofia Moreno <sofia@acme.com>

Cc: Amit Rao <amit@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sunrise notice activation — initial redline asks

Marissa —

Thanks for the demo last week. Legal and procurement reviewed the MSA/order form and sent a short set of asks focused on term mechanics before we can get procurement sign-off. The core items are:

- Auto-renew: Acme requests an explicit opt-out activation (we want the customer to be able to affirmatively opt-out instead of silent renewal).
- Notice window: procurement is asking for a 120-day advance notice for renewal cancellation for our enterprise accounts.
- Termination for convenience: request for a 60-day termination-for-convenience right for either party with a short transition payment (tiered by remaining committed months).

I attached an XLSX that maps their ask to the MSA sections (Acme_Term_Requests.xlsx). Can Redwood legal/ops confirm whether these are acceptable or if you need counter language?

We have an internal deadline to complete the contract routing by July 6. If we can align this week, procurement will push to countersign.

—Sofia
Sofia Moreno
Sr. Manager, Vendor Ops | Acme Corp

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Moreno <sofia@acme.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sunrise notice activation — initial redline asks

Sofia —

Thanks for the clear matrix and the deadline callout. Looping in Karthik (legal) and Laura (sales operations) — they’ll lead the redline response. A few quick notes from product/ops perspective:

- Opt-out activation: we are okay with an affirmative opt-out flow, but we typically implement an opt-out windows and a documented opt-in/opt-out audit trail to avoid accidental contract lapses.
- Notice window: 120 days is longer than our standard enterprise cadence (90 days), but not unreasonable for a global deployment. We’ll propose a compromise.
- Termination-for-convenience: we support mutual TFC but need to align on transition obligations and whether early termination fees are proportional to remaining committed term (we usually propose a three-tier scale).

Karthik — can you take the lead on drafting counter language? Laura, can you run an impact calc on committed capacity and expected TCV exposure if we accept a 120-day notice vs 90-day?

Possible timing: legal redlines by tomorrow EOD, internal commercial approval by Wednesday, then back to Acme with a consolidated response.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Head of Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
(attachment: Redwood_MSA_v3_redlines.pdf)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Moreno <sofia@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 14:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sunrise notice activation — proposed counter and alternatives

Sofia / Acme team —

Appreciate the level of detail in the spreadsheet. We reviewed and propose the following redline approach (high level):

1) Auto-renew / opt-out activation:
   - Counter-proposal: keep automatic renewal but require affirmative opt-out notice to be delivered at least 60 days prior to renewal date. We will include an audit log requirement showing delivery and acknowledgment.
   - Rationale: preserves business continuity for ongoing deployments while giving Acme an operational opt-out window.

2) Renewal notice window:
   - Counter-proposal: 90-day standard notice with a negotiated option to extend to 120 days for multi-region contracts with >$2M ARR.
   - Rationale: aligns with Redwood sales ops playbook and limits risk on capacity planning.

3) Termination for convenience (TFC):
   - Counter-proposal: mutual TFC with 90-day notice; early termination fee equal to remaining committed months pro-rated at 50% for months 1–3, 30% for months 4–6, 0% thereafter. Alternatively, Acme may choose a fixed transition fee equal to three months of committed run-rate.
   - Rationale: balances Acme’s desire for exit flexibility with Redwood’s need to cover reserved capacity costs for committed pools.

Attached: a tracked-redline PDF (Redwood_MSA_v3_redlines.pdf) and an internal model to quantify TCV exposure. If you prefer the 120-day notice as a hard term, we can discuss a credit or price concession to offset the operational buffer.

Proposed next steps:
- Acme to confirm whether the 90-day / 120-day tier model is acceptable or whether you need the 120-day blanket.
- If Acme prefers blanket 120-day, we’ll present a commercial offset (one-quarter run-rate credit amortized over the first 6 months post-sign).

Can we hop on a 30-minute call tomorrow to finalize? I’m available 10:00–11:30 PT.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Counsel, Contracts & Commercial | Redwood Inference
(attachment: Redwood_MSA_v3_redlines.pdf)

Subject: Re: Sunrise notice activation — agreed path forward

Karthik / Marissa —

Thanks for the thoughtful counter. Acme is comfortable with the hybrid approach you outlined with one caveat: procurement asks that the 120-day elevated notice bucket be available for this scope (multi-region + data residency) without a strict $2M ARR gate; our justification is the migration and cross-region compliance work that would be required.

Given our licensing forecast, we’re willing to accept the TFC fee scale you proposed (the tiered pro-rata percentages) but would like the fixed three-month transition fee to be explicitly available as an election for Acme.

We agree to the 90-day standard notice as the default, and to the 120-day elevated notice for the Sunrise deployment for Acme. We can add language that the elevated notice applies to named services and regions listed in the purchase order (that should be sufficient for our internal routing).

Next steps:
- We’ll upload a short PO and countersign request once you send the finalized redline PDF with the agreed language.
- Can Redwood legal insert the clause where the elevated 120-day notice applies to services enumerated in the order form?

If Marissa/Laura want to route a small commercial concession to help move procurement, we can accept a one-time implementation credit.

Thanks —
Sofia Moreno
Sr. Manager, Vendor Ops | Acme Corp
